result.name: Third-Party Vendor SLA Enforcement
result.business_requirement: The business requires legally binding Service Level Agreements with critical third-party vendors that mandate guaranteed uptime, rapid incident response, and financial penalties for service degradation.
result.business_objective: Mitigate operational downtime and reputational damage caused by failures in external dependencies beyond the platform's direct control.
result.business_value: Ensures service continuity and protects brand reputation by holding vendors accountable for performance, while preventing revenue loss from unavailability.
success_measures: 100% of critical vendors have active SLAs with defined penalty clauses
Average vendor incident response time meets proposed 1-hour target
Zero unplanned service outages exceeding proposed 15-minute threshold
policies_and_constraints: All SLAs must include clear definitions of uptime and response metrics
Penalty clauses must be enforceable under local jurisdiction laws
Vendors must provide real-time status reporting interfaces
assumptions: Critical vendors are identified based on current dependency mapping
Legal review is available to draft and approve contract terms
Vendors are willing to negotiate standard industry SLA terms
risks_and_dependencies: Vendors may refuse to accept financial penalty clauses
Ambiguity in SLA definitions could lead to disputes
Dependency on external vendors for core functions creates single points of failure

semantic.assessment_summary: The requirement clearly defines a business need for vendor accountability and risk mitigation. The success measures (100% SLA coverage, response time targets) are framed as contractual/operational goals rather than technical implementation details. No unsupported assumptions or contradictions found.
